technical_and_design_decisions: For U4 (Solo ordering service): Implement using Go's buffered channel with a single goroutine reading to create blocks. Use in-memory map for ledger. Implement a simple seek interface for clients to allow history discovery.
For U6 (State cache): Use a thread-safe cache (e.g., LRU cache with sync.RWMutex) to store read-set results during transaction simulation, reducing repeated DB accesses.

For U2 (Lifecycle system chaincode for deployment policies): Extend the existing lifecycle system chaincode to include deployment policy management as part of the chaincode definition, using protobuf messages for policy specification.

For U8 (Standalone CLI): Create a new Go binary (e.g., 'fabric-cli') that includes only the peer command logic, using build tags to exclude RocksDB and other heavy dependencies, and provide platform-specific builds for Mac and Windows.
assumptions: The developer is experienced with Hyperledger Fabric codebase and Go programming language.
Existing codebase structure is modifiable without significant refactoring.
Documentation tasks (U3, U7) involve writing or updating Markdown files in the existing documentation repository.
GitHub mirror (U5) can be set up using standard mirroring scripts and CI pipeline (e.g., Jenkins or GitHub Actions).
All estimates are for a single developer performing design, coding, unit testing, and basic integration testing. No separate QA or code review effort is included.
Effort estimates assume moderate complexity and no major unforeseen obstacles.

activities.activity_description: Add a friendly name field to chaincode registration and deployment, update CLI commands, protobuf definitions, and persistence layer to support storing and retrieving the friendly name. Includes unit tests.

activities.activity_name: Implement lifecycle system chaincode for deployment policies
activities.activity_description: Design and implement a lifecycle system chaincode that manages deployment policies for chaincodes. Modify existing chaincode lifecycle to support policy specification, validation, and enforcement. Includes unit and integration tests.
Research existing upgrade flows and write comprehensive documentation covering chaincode upgrade, peer upgrade, and ordering service upgrade. Include examples and best practices.

Implement a simple ordering service type 'solo' with a single process. Use a buffered channel and single goroutine to create batches/blocks. Implement in-memory ledger for history and a seek interface for clients. Includes unit and integration tests.

activities.activity_name: Set up GitHub mirror for Hyperledger Fabric code
activities.activity_description: Create a GitHub repository mirroring the Gerrit repository, configure automated sync script, set up CI pipeline (e.g., GitHub Actions) to run basic checks. Update documentation for new repository location.

activities.activity_name: Implement state cache for read-write set building
activities.activity_description: Add a thread-safe cache (e.g., LRU) to store state data during transaction simulation, reducing repeated database reads. Integrate into the transaction manager and ensure cache invalidation on commit. Includes unit tests.
Work with documentation team to update hyperledger.org website to prominently link to Hyperledger Fabric documentation. Add cross-references and ensure all project docs are easily findable.

activities.activity_name: Extract peer CLI into standalone binary
activities.activity_description: Refactor peer command code to remove dependencies on validating peer internals like RocksDB. Create a new Go binary 'fabric-cli' with platform-specific builds for Mac and Windows. Update build scripts and documentation.
Perform end-to-end integration tests combining all changes, fix any issues, update version numbers, prepare release notes, and tag the release.
